questions.question:
Prove that, for $0 \le x \le 1$,
$$\cos^{-1}\left(\sqrt{x}\right)=\frac12\cos^{-1}\left(2x-1\right)$$
questions.answer:
Let $\theta = \cos^{-1}\left(\sqrt{x}\right)$. Since $0 \le \sqrt{x} \le 1$, we have $0 \le \theta \le \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $\cos\theta = \sqrt{x}$.

Using the double-angle formula,
$$\cos 2\theta = 2\cos^2\theta - 1 = 2\left(\sqrt{x}\right)^2 - 1 = 2x - 1.$$

Since $0 \le 2\theta \le \pi$, which is the range of $\cos^{-1}$, it follows that
$$2\theta = \cos^{-1}(2x-1) \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \cos^{-1}\left(\sqrt{x}\right) = \theta = \frac12\cos^{-1}(2x-1). \qquad \blacksquare$$

(The range check is essential: $\cos 2\theta = 2x-1$ alone only gives $2\theta = \cos^{-1}(2x-1)$ because $2\theta$ lies in $[0,\pi]$.)

questions.question:
(b) Using the result $\cos(A-B) - \cos(A+B) = 2\sin A \sin B$ from part (a), or otherwise, prove by mathematical induction that, for $n \ge 1$,
$$\sin\theta + \sin(3\theta) + \cdots + \sin\big((2n-1)\theta\big) = \frac{\sin^2(n\theta)}{\sin\theta}.$$
questions.answer:
(Assume $\sin\theta \ne 0$, so the right-hand side is defined.)

**Base case $n=1$.** LHS $= \sin\theta$. RHS $= \dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{\sin\theta} = \sin\theta$. True for $n=1$.

**Inductive step.** Assume true for $n=k$:
$$\sin\theta + \sin 3\theta + \cdots + \sin\big((2k-1)\theta\big) = \frac{\sin^2(k\theta)}{\sin\theta}.$$
Prove true for $n=k+1$, i.e. that the sum up to $\sin\big((2k+1)\theta\big)$ equals $\dfrac{\sin^2\big((k+1)\theta\big)}{\sin\theta}$.

$$\text{LHS} = \frac{\sin^2(k\theta)}{\sin\theta} + \sin\big((2k+1)\theta\big) = \frac{\sin^2(k\theta) + \sin\theta\,\sin\big((2k+1)\theta\big)}{\sin\theta}.$$

By part (a) with $A = (2k+1)\theta$, $B = \theta$:
$$\sin\big((2k+1)\theta\big)\sin\theta = \tfrac12\big[\cos(2k\theta) - \cos\big((2k+2)\theta\big)\big].$$
Also $\sin^2(k\theta) = \tfrac12\big[1 - \cos(2k\theta)\big]$. So the numerator is
$$\tfrac12\big[1-\cos(2k\theta)\big] + \tfrac12\big[\cos(2k\theta) - \cos\big(2(k+1)\theta\big)\big] = \tfrac12\big[1 - \cos\big(2(k+1)\theta\big)\big] = \sin^2\big((k+1)\theta\big).$$

Hence LHS $= \dfrac{\sin^2\big((k+1)\theta\big)}{\sin\theta}$ = RHS, so the result is true for $n=k+1$.

By mathematical induction, the result is true for all integers $n \ge 1$.

prev.question: Show that $\cos(A-B) - \cos(A+B) = 2\sin A \sin B$.
prev.answer: $$\begin{aligned}\cos(A-B)-\cos(A+B) &= (\cos A\cos B + \sin A\sin B) - (\cos A\cos B - \sin A \sin B)\\ &= 2\sin A\sin B\end{aligned}$$
